tagline: Leading European airline group connecting people and places
hero_kpi_rationale: Operating profit is IAG's primary performance indicator, reflecting the profitability of its airline operations following post-pandemic restructuring and amid high volatility in fuel and labor costs. A significant rebound to €1,197.7 million in 2024 from €129.5 million in 2023 demonstrates the strength of air traffic recovery, with an 826% year-on-year increase.
company_description: International Consolidated Airlines Group S.A., together with its subsidiaries, engages in the provision of passenger and cargo transportation services in the North Atlantic, Latin America, the Caribbean, Europe, Africa, the Middle East, South Asia, the Asia Pacific, and internationally. It operates through British Airways, Iberia, Vueling, Aer Lingus, and IAG Loyalty segments. The company manufactures, repairs, maintains, overhauls, retrofits, repurposes, upgrades aircraft, and aircraft parts and equipment. In addition, it provides airline operations, insurance, aircraft leasing, aircraft maintenance, tour operation, air freight operations, call center, ground handling, trustee, retail, IT, finance, flight procurement, storage, aircraft technical assistance, human resources support, and airport infrastructure development services; and manages airline loyalty reward currency. The company was incorporated in 2009 and is headquartered in Harmondsworth, the United Kingdom.

kpis.name: Operating Profit
kpis.explanation: Profit generated from core operations before taxes.
kpis.description: Operating profit increased from €129.5 million in 2023 to €1,197.681 million in 2024, driven by strong recovery in air traffic and disciplined cost management.
kpis.signal: Significant rebound in operating profit in 2024 following a challenging 2023.

kpis.name: Net Profit
kpis.explanation: Profit after all expenses, taxes, and financial charges.
kpis.description: Net profit reached €941.797 million in 2024 compared to a loss of €22.749 million in 2023, marking a significant improvement in the group's financial health.
kpis.signal: Return to net profitability in 2024 after a loss in 2023.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from the group's core services.
kpis.description: Revenue surged from €6,448.993 billion in 2023 to €31,464.314 billion in 2024, reflecting strong demand for air travel and increased operational capacity.
kpis.signal: Very strong revenue growth in 2024, driven by air traffic recovery.

kpis.name: Cash and Equivalents
kpis.explanation: Available liquidity to meet operational needs.
kpis.description: Cash and equivalents increased from €1,354.219 billion in 2023 to €2,382.220 billion in 2024, supported by cash flow generation and debt financing.
kpis.signal: Significant increase in cash, strengthening financial resilience.

kpis.name: Net Debt
kpis.explanation: Total financial debt minus available cash.
kpis.description: Net debt stood at €7,961.432 billion in 2024 versus €8,117.521 billion in 2023 (based on total debt of €10,343.652 billion in 2024 minus cash of €2,382.220 billion), reflecting refinancing of short- and long-term debt.
kpis.signal: Relatively stable debt level despite increased activity.

kpis.name: Employee Costs
kpis.explanation: Expenses related to salaries, social charges, and other personnel costs.
kpis.description: Employee costs rose from €1,965.920 billion in 2023 to €2,586.967 billion in 2024, reflecting workforce redeployment with traffic growth and improved compensation.
kpis.signal: Increase in employee costs linked to operational recovery and workforce expansion.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €42.85 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of €14.27 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Total dividend payment per share over the fiscal year.
kpis.description: Five-year history (2021-2025). Source: yfinance ex-div dates.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Annual total: dividends paid + share buybacks.
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends and buybacks (2021-2025) in billion GBp. Source: yfinance cashflow.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Portion of net profit distributed. >80% = potentially unsustainable.

kpis.name: Earnings Per Share
kpis.explanation: Net profit divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares during the fiscal year. Measures the company's ability to generate profit per share: basis for Payout Ratio (DPS / EPS).
kpis.description: Five-year history (2021-2025). Source: yfinance income statement (Diluted EPS).

risks.title: Dependence on strategic airline partners
risks.summary: IAG relies heavily on strategic partnerships with other airlines to expand its network and enhance competitiveness. A disruption or weakening of these alliances could limit its international reach.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned in the group's strategic context, with strong language affirming the importance of partnerships. The trend is stable, and the category is central to the business model.

risks.title: Intense competition on international routes
risks.summary: IAG faces increasing competition from major international carriers on long-haul routes, particularly via hubs such as London and Madrid, threatening its market share and profitability.
risks.score_rationale: The document highlights competitive pressure in global markets, with strong language on the need to maintain leadership positions. Recurring and strategic risk.

risks.title: Exposure to Qatar Airways' decisions
risks.summary: As a significant shareholder, Qatar Airways may influence certain strategic or governance decisions, potentially creating conflicts of interest with other IAG shareholders.
risks.score_rationale: Qatar Airways is identified as a significant shareholder. The risk is moderate in intensity but strategic, with a recurring presence in disclosures.

risks.title: Cybersecurity of booking systems
risks.summary: The growing reliance on digital services and booking platforms exposes IAG to cyberattacks that could disrupt operations and compromise sensitive passenger data.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is implicit in digital investments and customer data management. Although not explicitly stated, it is inferred from the group's IT and digital priorities.

risks.title: Dependence on synergies between group airlines
risks.summary: IAG's performance depends heavily on its ability to achieve cost savings and harmonize operations across its various airline subsidiaries, which is complex to implement.
risks.score_rationale: The model relies on capturing synergies between British Airways, Iberia, Vueling, etc. The language emphasizes this strategic priority, with a stable trend.

risks.title: Increased regulation of airline mergers
risks.summary: External growth projects, such as the acquisition of Air Europa, are subject to strict regulatory scrutiny, with risks of blocking by European antitrust authorities.
risks.score_rationale: The document mentions costs related to the failed Air Europa acquisition, indicating a stringent regulatory environment. Strong language and an upward trend.

risks.title: Management of key group talent
risks.summary: IAG depends on the performance and stability of its key executives and managers, particularly to drive transformation plans and maintain an aligned corporate culture.
risks.score_rationale: The document emphasizes leadership and group culture. The loss of senior executives or strategic talent could impact transformation.

risks.title: Reputation related to regulatory disputes
risks.summary: IAG faces several legal and regulatory proceedings in various countries, the outcomes of which could harm its reputation and result in public sanctions.
risks.score_rationale: Ongoing disputes are mentioned (€3.5 million in contingent liabilities), with potential impact on brand image. Trend is stable, but risk is recurring.

ai_positioning.summary: IAG does not mention any strategic initiatives related to artificial intelligence in its recent financial reports. The company does not position AI as a lever for transformation or competitiveness.
evidence: No mention of AI in the 2024 annual report
Absence of AI-related KPIs or projects in the Business and MD&A sections
No reference to automation or predictive analytics tools
